plan:
- High-performance System-on-Chip (SoC) with multi-core ARM CPU and integrated GPU, suitable for mobile applications. Selection will depend on power efficiency and computational needs for extreme RAM/storage.
- 128GB LPDDR5/6 RAM modules integrated directly with the SoC for maximum bandwidth. Requires custom PCB design for density.
- 3TB NVMe SSD storage solution, potentially multiple high-density M.2 modules or custom embedded flash, connected via high-speed interfaces.
- High-resolution AMOLED or OLED display, multi-camera system (wide, ultra-wide, telephoto), and full suite of communication modules (5G, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.x, GPS).
- Advanced power management ICs, high-capacity Li-Po battery pack (e.g., 5000-8000mAh), and rapid charging circuitry (USB-C Power Delivery).
- Precision-machined aluminum or titanium unibody chassis, internal mounting points for components, custom-designed thermal management system (vapor chamber, graphite sheets).

subSteps.title: 3D print all custom mounts and the vibration motor mount
Deburr and clean 3D printed parts, ensure fitment for respective components
Clean all glass panels and lens covers
Connect Main SoC to LPDDR6 RAM and UFS Storage via flex cables (if not integrated)
Connect AMOLED Display, Cameras, Wireless Module, GNSS, Audio Codec, and Sensors to Main SoC/PCB via flex cables
Connect USB-C PD Controller to Main SoC and route VBUS to Power Management IC
Connect Power Management IC to all power-consuming components and Li-Po Battery
Connect Linear Haptic Vibrator to Power Management IC and Main SoC (PWM control)
Perform initial continuity checks on all power and ground lines
Connect Li-Po Battery and apply power to the main PCB assembly
Verify power rails and voltages using a multimeter
Flash initial firmware/bootloader to Main SoC via USB-C or debug port
Test basic display functionality and touch input (if integrated with display)
Verify camera module detection and capture functionality for all cameras
Test Wireless (5G/Wi-Fi/BT) and GNSS module functionality
Verify sensor functionality (accelerometer, gyro, magnetometer, ambient light, fingerprint)
Test audio input (MIC) and output (SPK) via audio codec
Mount Main SoC, RAM, Storage, Wireless, GNSS, Audio, USB-C Controller, and Sensors into their respective 3D printed mounts and secure mounts to internal midframe with M1.2 screws
Apply thermal paste to Main SoC and attach vapor chamber to internal midframe, then affix graphite thermal sheets
Mount linear haptic vibrator into its 3D printed mount and secure to internal midframe
Adhere Li-Po Battery to internal midframe using the battery adhesive strip
Install USB-C port gasket, speaker grills, power button, volume rocker, and SIM tray into the unibody chassis
Install internal midframe assembly into the unibody chassis and secure with M1.2 screws
Attach main, ultrawide, and telephoto camera modules with gaskets to internal midframe and secure respective lens covers to the rear glass panel, then adhere rear glass panel to unibody chassis
Attach front camera module with its lens cover, apply display adhesive seal, and carefully secure the AMOLED display and display glass panel to the unibody chassis

projectDescription: The Apex Smartphone is a flagship mobile device integrating a powerful SoC with 128GB of LPDDR6 RAM and an unprecedented 3TB of UFS 4.0 storage. It features a multi-camera system, advanced connectivity, and robust thermal management within a precision-machined unibody chassis.

assumptions: All electrical components are pre-assembled onto a main flexible PCB (FPCB) or rigid PCB, with interconnections designed for flex cables or ZIF connectors where applicable. No hand-soldering of SMD components is required.

The 'main_soc', 'integrated_ram', 'internal_storage', 'power_management_ic_main', 'wireless_module', 'gnss_module', 'audio_codec', 'accelerometer_gyro', 'magnetometer', 'ambient_light_proximity', 'fingerprint_sensor', and 'usb_c_controller' are factory-mounted on one or more PCBs.
The user has basic electronics assembly experience and familiarity with smartphone construction.
Required drivers and a host PC are available for initial bring-up and flashing.
